utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. On this Monday, the 5th of February, I'd like to say good afternoon to everybody in the courtroom, to the Prosecution, the Defence counsel, the accused, and everybody else. I'm going to give the floor to Madam Registrar straight away for some IC numbers to start off with.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, Prosecution has submitted four lists of documents. The first list to be tendered through Witness Omer Dilberovic will be given number IC 323. The second list to be tendered through Witness DB will be given number IC 324 under seal. The third list to be tendered through Witness Dzevad Hadzizukic already given IC 325. The fourth list to be tendered through Witness Heljic will be given number IC 326. Defence 3 has also submitted four lists of documents. The first to be tendered through Witness DB. That will be given IC 327. The list tendered through Witness Anel Heljic will be become IC 328. The next one tendered through Witness Dzevad Hadzizukic will be given IC number 329. And the fourth which is an opposition to admission of evidence tendered through Witness Dzevad Hadzizukic will be given IC number 330. Furthermore, would I like to make a clarification regarding last Thursday's transcript dated 1st of February, 2007. During OTP's re-examination, on page 13383, line 20 of the transcript, Mr. Scott asked for the photograph bearing number IC 303. In fact, we were looking at IC 304. On page 13384, line 9, Mr. Scott asked the witness to look at IC 304, but in fact we were looking at IC 305. And finally, on page 13384, line 18 to 22, where it was unclear if we were looking at IC 305 or IC 302, in fact we were looking at IC 303. Thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar, for the explanations you gave us. Before we carry on with the witness testimonies, I'd like to go back to a confusion that arose at the end of last week. When the witness left the room, Counsel Tomic got up to tell us that she wasn't able to ask her questions, and I remember that Counsel Tomic did in fact get up on her feet and then sat down, after which I gave the floor to the Prosecution for the re-examination, and the Prosecution went on to ask those questions, and I thanked the witness for coming in to testify. When the witness had left, Counsel Tomic told us that she wasn't able to ask her questions on behalf of her client, Mr. Coric. And then in the transcript -- we read out the questions in the transcript and for the transcript the questions that she wanted to ask. We looked into those questions during the weekend, we examined them, and it appears that most of those questions were already broached and dealt with during the cross-examination by other counsel and that the essential point as far as the Chamber is concerned is to know whether when the sniper was in the house or fired from the house, whether there was a flash and whether the witness could have seen the flash from the sniper fire. The expert witness who will be coming sometime after tomorrow will be able to answer that question. So there is no absolute need to put any additional questions to the witness. And let me repeat that he answered this question several times saying that he saw the flash. Nevertheless, if Counsel Tomic would like to have the witness recalled to answer her questions, I shall ask the Defence to put it in writing and then we will give a ruling on the request made in writing for that. But as I say, I think that when the expert witness comes in they will be able to address your preoccupations. Now, we're a little -- running a little late because two witnesses were supposed to be last week and we didn't have time, so we're going to hear them now. And I'd like to ask the Prosecution to accelerate the proceedings as much as possible. We have the third witness today and the fourth will come in tomorrow afternoon. Is that right, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. That is correct. We will pick up where we left off last week. I would hope that we can get through three of those witnesses today and move the second witness that was scheduled for today until tomorrow to be followed immediately by the expert witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let's move into private session for a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, would you please stand to take the solemn declaration. And can you give me your name, surname, and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you a profession, sir, current occupation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have you ever testified before an international or national Tribunal on the events that took place in your country or is this the first time that you're testifying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, would you now go ahead and read the solemn declaration presented to you by the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. You may be seated. Some explanations from me to begin with. You're going to be first of all answering questions put to you by the Prosecution. The Prosecution might also be presenting you with certain documents, and after that first stage we come to stage two, which is the Defence counsel and the cross-examination. They will be asking you questions. The Judges sitting in front of you can also ask you questions at any time if they think it necessary. The Defence will have one hour, but it would be advisable if the Defence can reduce that time, and we would be very grateful to them because we have three witnesses coming in today. Mr. Mundis, without further ado, I give you the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Before I read the summary of the witness's written evidence, I neglected to mention that I am accompanied today by our intern Aleksandra Bojovic. I'm taking the summary from the 65 ter summary in early 2006. The witness lived in West Mostar in July 1993. When the witness was 12 the Croatian Defence Council arrested his father and detained him in Heliodrom. The witness and his mother moved to another part of West Mostar. A month later the Croatian Defence Council expelled the witness and his family after robbing them of their valuables. The Croatian Defence Council soldiers took seven or eight Muslim families in a van to Bulevar near the confrontation lines and told them to cross towards the armija Bosnia-Herzegovina positions. During the crossing the witness and his grandfather were told to carry the dead bodies of two males to the Muslim side. Witness and his family then lived in Donja Mahala, East Mostar, which was under constant shelling and firing by the Croatian Defence Council. Muslim civilians lived in shelters. In September 1993, the witness went home and was returning to the shelter through safe route of small alleys. However, there were open spots which had to be crossed which snipers had a clear view of. Orucevica Sokak was one of these with snipers in Stotina. The witness crossed this spot almost every day. He and 14-year-old Neno clearly children in civilian clothes started to run across the four metres of open ground. A bullet hit Neno in his arm and then hit the witness in the stomach. Neno was sniped again in the hip and fell down. The witness turned back and tried to pull Neno in safety. When he tried to grab Neno, he felt that something went through his hair and right after that something else scratched the inside of his left upper arm. The witness realised that the sniper was still shooting and got so scared that he did not dare to pull Neno in safety. The witness ran to the infirmary to get a stretcher to transport Neno. At the infirmary he noticed that he was wounded too. After surgery in the war hospital, witness took about two months to recover.

utterances.text: Yes. It's not very clear, but yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if it would be helpful, we do have a still of this photograph as well that we can ask the witness to mark, or if that's not necessary we can move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness should put his initials on document 334. He forgot to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have a question I'd like to put to you, because we have just seen the 360-degree photograph. And when I saw it, I was wondering whether the shot could have been fired from two other directions. You're quite categorical about the fact that the fire -- that the shot was fired from the house that you were pointed out to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And on what basis do you make such a claim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we know that the sniper opened fire from that position. There were three houses in Stotina where you can't see one in the photograph because it's a little further away, and the direction of the bullet led us to believe that the bullet must have been fired from that house in Stotina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You say "we knew." Was this a well-known fact in the area that there was a sniper who was in that house in Stotina? Did everyone know about that? And is that why everyone was so careful when they went out into the space that you have pointed out to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I would like to put also a question to you, Mr. Katica. At the moment in the video when you show your first wounds, it seemed to me that your right hand was on the upper right part of your belly and with your left hand you reached behind at the spot further down above your hip. Did these points mark the entry and exit of the bullet or is it just an accident that you had one hand in the area of your kidneys?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I pointed to the entry and exit wound.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Finally, Mr. Katica, if you could please look at the screen. We have another image that's contained on P 09139. Do you see that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, what's depicted in the lower half of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: You can see the house that I marked just a minute ago in the other photograph, the house from which the sniper opened fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again with the assistance of the usher we have a still that's been captured from this photograph and I would ask the witness: Sir, if you could take the black marker and circle the house that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if you could please put your initials, sir, on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And just for the record, I mean the photograph is highly suggest when you do have a red marker there. We might as well just put an arrow and say is this the house. I mean, it's just really rather suggestive, I would say. And I know I'm dealing with professional Judges, but even in this context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Witness, this house that you have pointed to, why do you claim that this is the house that the sniper was hidden in? Do you have any additional information you could provide us with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm saying that was the case because it's only from that position that he could have opened fire on us. And people said that there was a sniper in that house. People would see him open fire at night. It's only from that position, only from that direction that the bullet could have hit us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time, because according to the document from the hospital you left on the 4th of October. Apparently you went to hospital on the 1st of October. So it was towards the end of September that you were hit. But at the time who controlled the house, the HVO or the ABiH? Tell us if you know and, if not, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The HVO controlled it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Madam Registrar, could we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 335.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, it would perhaps be good to wrap this up now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Defence then has an hour at the most. If you can use less time, that would be even better. Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do have a few questions to pose to the gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated that everybody knew that that was the house that where so-called snipers were operating under; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I take it the -- the army of BiH, they had their own snipers?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Are you sure about that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I'm sure that I don't know whether the armija had its own snipers. I can't say that it did, and I can't say that it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not asking you where they were. Are you suggesting here under oath to these Judges that while you lived there you didn't know that the army of BiH had snipers operating on that side of the confrontation line? Yes, no?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: As to whether I knew or not, well, I don't know. They were probably there but I didn't see them. That's what I said. I didn't see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But you're not suggesting that they were not operating, they didn't a snipers?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I'm not making such a claim. I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. I'm confused a little bit. Let me out here. You either know that there were snipers or there were not snipers. Now, are you suggesting under oath here, okay, and I'm stressing "under oath" because you could be penalised for that. Are you stressing under oath that you had no knowledge that there were snipers on the Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Even if there were snipers they didn't open fire on us. I don't know where they were, but they probably were somewhere. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, I'm not asking whether they opened fire on you. I want to make sure that I get a clear answer from you that there were snipers working on the Muslim side. Yes or no? To your knowledge.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Fair enough. Fair enough. All right. Now, if everybody knew that this house was a sniper house, I suspect that if there were snipers working on the Muslim side, a matter which you're unsure of, although you say probably now, they would know where to fire at to take out the snipers; right? Kind of complicated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. You're really asking the witness to make all sort of supposition and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: How?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: -- and assumptions. "You think they would have done this." How is the witness supposed to give a testimony about what possibly existing ABiH snipers would perhaps have done if they had known this or thus that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm glad ---

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You would criticise this if someone else did it, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad that you asked the question, Your Honour because, you see, I sat there and I listened to the gentleman say, "There we all knew. We all knew." I didn't hear a question from you, Your Honour, saying, "Tell us sir, exactly, concretely, how, sir, did you know." So here he is speculating that we all knew. Where is the concreteness? And I pose the question that if people knew that this was such a notorious place where snipers were working out of, why didn't anybody react to it? That's the whole point of the exercise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So if you knew, the army of BiH would have known, if you were just a citizen? May I put it that way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question that counsel is asking you is something that I gave thought to this weekend. How come, Witness, because you're not the first person to speak to us about that house, apparently the house was well-known as a place where there was a sniper, so how come the BiH did not attack that house, did not fire at that house, did not send a rocket to blow it up? Have you got an explanation or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. Much more articulate than my question was, but exactly the point I was trying to drive home at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. Answer my question first, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Donja Mahala where I lived during the war and where I live to this day, where there was an open space and where you could see the house from, that's where the sniper shot, where you could see the house at Stotina. Now, whether the BH army shot at the house are didn't, I don't know. I was a child. I was in a shelter, and it was rarely that we saw a soldier. And if we saw a soldier they would be with ordinary rifles. I just said I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you were wounded together with your friend, and you were taken to a hospital straight away belonging to the BH army because it says -- the document says a hospital of the BH army. I assume that they asked you where you were wounded, and you probably said, "I was wounded in such-and-such a locality." And now the question that I'm asking myself is, how come the BH army didn't send a sniper for their part, a commando or whoever else, to go and destroy that particular house? Do you have an explanation for that, or is there none? Is it that it was a war and things like that? Because one gains the impression, sir, and we listened to the testimony of a number of victims telling us that there were sniper shots, sniper fire, and we can localise the places, but one wonders that afterwards nothing happened. So you, since you were a victim yourself and lived in the area, and you left on the 4th of October so you probably returned to that district, that nothing happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing happened -- or, rather, I don't know. I was operated on in the hospital, and when I left I was at home for almost a month recuperating.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would have liked to have asked my question before our Presiding Judge, Judge Antonetti, asks his question. It is my impression and I would like to ask the witness if he may confirm that, that he was a 12-year-old child at that time. And I believe that it is what the starting point should be if we are asking him questions. And definitely in my view some of the questions went beyond that very important issue of what was his age, the witness's age at that time. And of course later on he might have known. He might have got some more information what the snipers' activity was on both sides, but I believe in the present case his not to testify about what later on he knows about sniper activities in general, but the issue is now what kind of present -- I mean, in his case, what kind of happenings were what he were able to note. That is why I would say that the issue is that what he thought the direction of the shot was come from, and it is not that what he thought about, if the BH army had sniper activities. So I would like to ask the witness, that's why, to confirm or deny that in his view and in the -- in his knowledge when he was shot from what direction the entry wound was effected in his body and what was his you view of that time about the major direction where the shot had come -- has come. It is my question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you heard what the Judge said. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the entrance/exit wound was such that I can only claim that the -- that the firing had come from Stotina, that it had been shot from Stotina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Just a couple of more questions. We saw a lot of photographs here, some that you circled and initialed. Now, those photographs, they don't depict -- they're not a fair and accurate depiction of that area as it was on the day that you were shot; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: The alleyway didn't look like it did on the photograph. The street didn't look like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But there were also it would appear to me at least that some of the buildings might have been fixed or even were built up since that period of time; correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: You mean the buildings which I claim that the sniper fire came from?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All sorts of buildings, not just that one.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, yes. Most of them had been fixed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But we don't have any photographs today for you to look at and show to us that are a fair and accurate depiction of that location on the day that you were shot so at least we could trace back to see whether the shooter had an unobstructed view, wherever he might have been, and also to look at the universe of possibilities where the shots might have been able to come from. We don't have that today, do we?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I'm sure the -- I'm sure the Judges understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Karnavas. Mr. Murphy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We have no questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, counsel. Next counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Mr. Praljak, with your permission, would like to ask a few questions. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honours, shall I start off or are we going to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have the break afterwards. Perhaps we'll need to rest after having heard your questions. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask you some technical questions. May we have on the Elmo 3D 00748. It is a photograph 3D 220644. So 3D 00748 and the photograph is 3D 220644. Until that comes up on our screens let me ask you this: You were 12 years old at the time. That's not a lot but it's not little either. So at that time, did you know that Donja Mahala was the first defence line of the BiH army in defending its part of Mostar. Did you know that at that time?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: But the place that I was wounded at --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you the questions. We won't go into that now. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] That's not the right photograph. 3D 22-0644 is the number I would like, 3D 22-0644.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, when you were a 12-year-old child at the time, in walking down the alleyways and streets did you see the BH army, soldiers of the BH army armed? Did you see them walking around and going up to the lines they were defending?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I said a moment ago we would see them from time to time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, my next question is this, this is something that His Honour asked you: We looked at some documents and heard that at the end of September when you were wounded, from the 20th of September there was a large-scale offensive - and I'm asking you whether you know anything about that - in which the BH army took part of human so on. Do you know any of that, anything about that operation? Did you hear any shooting, any advance on the BH army side? When you were a child, did you know anything about that, that they had taken part of Hum at that time?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, I did hear shooting, but we were in the shelter so we didn't have any information on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the 30th of September a truce was signed, but do you know that -- did you know that -- it is possible to take Hum without taking Stotina, so that part of Hum was taken control of? You were a child. Of course you needn't know anything about this, but do you have to pass Stotina to get to Hum if you want to take control of Hum? Do you know that today or did you know that then?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: From this point in time I can say that it would be easiest to get there by going through Stotina. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Now may we have the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, we don't seem to have your photograph on e-court. Do you have the photograph yourself? Perhaps we can place it on the overhead projector if you do. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I have been informed that the photographs are on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. We did inform the client that the pictures are loaded in the e-court, but obviously not yet. They are. We're checking on the list. They are on the list. They are loaded. But perhaps Mr. Praljak can give his copy to ELMO. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] A copy, yes, but it's much nicer to see it in colour on our screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course it is but if we haven't got one --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: We have it directly from the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Counsel would you give us the number again because the one he gave us definitely is not the right one. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] 3D 00748, and then 3D 22-0644. Those are the numbers I have. But let's move on not to waste time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it will be of assistance if I say it's page 53 in 3D 00748. So the page is 3D 22-0644, or if you take the pages in order, it is page -- at page 53.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry, but here the last page is page 23 and bears number 3D 22-0614. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] We'll be able to see everything even with these copies placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Witness, I'd just like to complete my questioning. That is the house at Stotina. We discussed this issue at great length. Is that the building? Is that the house from which you claim or assume that the sniper shot when you were wounded?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I can't say because this isn't a very clear picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A moment ago you saw that same building, and we've shown it umpteen times so far. You saw the same building marked in red on the Prosecutor's photograph. It is a building at Stotina that has been identified a number of times, and a witness whose name I can't tell you now testified that the upper floor of that particular building during the war did not exist. There was no upper floor. However, as we've seen a picture of this house five times already as being the house where the sniping fire came from, can you see on the house the quantity of bullets that hit that house? Can you see the large number of bullets fired at that house?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And now this uppermost story, could we assume it was hit by a bullet or not?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, I can't see properly. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on the right-hand building, the other one -- you can take up the photograph in your hands and take a close look at it. Pick the photograph up. Pick the photograph up and take a good look at it and tell us whether there are a large number of holes where the bullets hit the house.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I can't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. You can't see. Then let's move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, on the photograph that Mr. Praljak is showing us, I can see, and take note that there are traces of bullets when they impacted on the house, around the windows.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean on the big house?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I said I saw the traces on that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, if you take a good look at what you marked on the Prosecution photograph as the Stotina area, do you agree that the building you marked in there and that this building are the same building?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: They seem to be the same ones, but I can't say for sure because I can't see where they're situated. I haven't got the whole aerial view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, the photograph that you're showing us, what year was that taken, because the Prosecution photograph is a recent one, whereas your one seems to be much older. So what year was that photograph taken? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] It was taken recently. Not a long time ago, no. Nothing much changed there. I took the photograph -- well, I don't know if it was this one or some other ones. When I looked into the problem of the destruction of the old bridge, that's when I made the photographs. But it is clear that hundreds, not to say thousands of bullets hit that building and we can see the traces. But let's move on to the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the same photograph, and you can see that the uppermost storey has been added on, and that is what one the witnesses also said. We'll find another photograph to show that this building and the one identified by the witness on the Prosecution photograph is one and the same. May I have the next photograph, please. Do you recognise this as being Stotina? This is a little right from the building I mentioned, turned towards Hum. Do you recognise that area?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I assume that's Stotina. It looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. That's Stotina. Now, do you see that pole on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] May I have the next photograph now, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And behind the pole you saw that small house. Let's return to the previous photograph again. Witness, to the right of the pole, can you see that small house there? Do you see a small house over there?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Now let's have the next photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the pole which is facing east. Look at the number of bullet traces on just an ordinary electric wire pole. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you as a 12-year-old boy, do you remember the amount of ammunition fired from the east as well, because -- would you agree with me that we're looking at the pole from the east?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: That's what it looks like, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, do you agree that there are dozens of traces of strong projectile impacts, not just ordinary calibre ones but higher calibre ones as well? Would you agree with me there?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes, I would. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] May we have a look at the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here it is. That is a view from Stotina; is that right? Do you agree with me there?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And on the right you see these residential buildings, do you?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Is what I'm going to say correct, that those residential buildings were built before the war, regardless of whether people had moved into them and so on? But they were as tall as they are now, that they were built before?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, these buildings were under construction, and we as children called them the construction sites, but they weren't finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. They hadn't -- construction hadn't been completed but they had reached roof level?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: No, they hadn't reached roof level.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, on this photograph could you show us where your alleyway is?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I can't show you that from here, from this angle of vision and from this photograph. I don't see where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, do you see these two twin buildings that are referred to as Sokol? Is it to the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, give us a rough estimate of where that alleyway would be. We have time. Think about it, and see if you can't show us your alleyway on that photograph.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I can't say. I really can't find it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is the position of the sniper shooting at you. When you say looking at it from the alleyway you saw a building and the house was white on a photograph showed by the Prosecutor, whereas I showed you a photograph which is not all white because there was a darker area of bricks on the top floor, but try. Your alleyway, did it run parallel to the -- these two buildings that we refer to as the Sokol buildings or not? Try and take up your pencil and indicate the alleyway. Does it run from Hum down the Neretva or what direction?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Orucevica alleyway should look like this. It runs this way. There are two entrances to the alleyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in what part of that alleyway were you hit? I'm sorry to have to ask you this, but where were you when you were hit on that path?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Very well. I have no more questions. Could we have IC numbers for these exhibits? Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, may we have the IC numbers, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will be IC 336.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We're going to take a 20-minute break and reconvene in 20 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll now resume. I'd like to greet Mr. Scott, and I will now give the floor to the next Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before I do so, Witness, there is a photograph on which you should mark your initials.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the accused. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Is the photograph that is Stotina according to the witness one that has also been given an IC number?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. IC 336, according to my understanding, covers all the photographs. Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, on the particular day you described you were on your way to a shelter because there was heavy shelling and firing. That was the starting point, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I was on my way to a shelter; yes, that's right. I had set off from home and was heading toward a shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. Just recapping your evidence in your statement that you confirm it was because of heavy shelling and firing. So what I want to get clear is that as you were crossing that very short gap where you say you and your friend were shot, was the -- the street that tree that we saw in the picture and the houses that you marked, you marked both of them and then you marked one of them, those were all down the street to your right, were they?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I haven't understood that. Could you repeat that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I'm just asking you to picture because you were there. You're crossing that short gap, the one where there's the telegraph pole, the very gap where you have described you and your friends -- friend as being shot. I just want to be clear. That tree and then beyond it down at the end of the road, the two houses on high ground that you were asked to look at on the photograph, as you went over that short piece of -- of the alleyway, the road, those were all down to your right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, yes. To the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes. And you gestured just then with your right hand to confirm that -- that it was. Now -- but it's equally clear, is it, I want to be absolutely plain because this is what we saw in the photographs and this is what you've described, that the entry wound is on your left-hand side, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So -- well, can we also get this clear: You say in your statement that at first you had no idea that you had been shot. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And what you did was you then -- because you appreciated that your friend Neno had been shot, you went to his parents' house. Now, how far away was his parents' house?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: It was a few minutes from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Could you give it in distance? Approximately is all I'm wanting, just in distance.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you went there, told them that Neno had been wounded, and then you returned, and by the time you got back there were people standing around Neno trying to bandage him. That's your evidence so far, and you're not -- you're confirming that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then somebody said that Neno should be taken to the infirmary, and you ran to the infirmary to get a stretcher. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And how far away was the infirmary from the point where Neno was -- well, he was presumably lying on the ground or sitting on the ground. How far was it from there to the infirmary?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Between 70 and a hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Do you remember what you were wearing? You said it was an autumn day. It was an ordinary autumn day as far as you remember. Were you wearing a T-shirt? Were you wearing a jacket? Do you have any memory of that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I was wearing the upper part of a tracksuit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So I just want to be clear that you go back and you are a 12-year-old boy who has had a bullet pass into the left-hand side of his body and out of the right-hand side of his body, who has then run to Neno's parents' house, run back, and these other people that were there with Neno, nobody notices that you've been wounded, presumably, because they send you to go and get the stretcher from the infirmary. Now, have you got that right so far, that nobody, including you, even noticed at that point that you had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: No one sent me to get the stretcher. I'd heard that a stretcher was needed and I went to fetch the stretcher. It was in the clinic that they noticed that I had been wounded. They saw the blood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That confirms, doesn't it, what I've just said. That is your evidence in your statement, that it was at the clinic that you first noticed. Confirm then you ran -- you ran, presumably. You ran to Neno's house. You ran back. It was you that was suggested or volunteered to go and get the stretcher from the infirmary. You ran off to the infirmary, and in all that time nobody, including you, even noticed that you had been shot so that a bullet had gone in one side of your stomach and out the other. That's right, is it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So in fact you don't even know whether you -- you don't know when, between the point that you arrived at the end of the alleyway and the point when you got to the infirmary, you don't even know when in that whole time you were shot, do you?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, that's more or less the case. All I felt was a certain burning sensation, but I didn't pay much attention to it. I ran to Neno's parents. I first tried to get him out and I couldn't. I ran to his parents' and then returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You said that the witness had been shot through his stomach. Did you want to say stomach or, rather, belly? Because it's not anatomically the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm afraid Your Honour with all due respect in cross-examining in English there is no distinction between those purposes of describing someone shot between the stomach and the belly but, Your Honour, I'm not going to quibble about it because we can see from the photographs where he was shot. It's not for you and me to enter into a etymological discussion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Your explanation is absolutely satisfactory. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I'm much obliged. That's the most important thing for me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So -- so can we get this -- would you agree with this: The one point, according to your recollection, when you could not have been shot in the way you describe was as you crossed the end of that small road, because you crossed with, according to you, the sniper hundreds of metres down the road to your right and yet you were shot in the left-hand side. So it obviously didn't happen at that point, did it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: No, that's when it happened. I was running across the proceed and I was facing the direction from which the bullet came. It was quite possible to determine the direction from which I had been hit. But at the time I didn't really feel the -- the shot. All I felt was this burning sensation. I didn't really pay much attention to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, let's get real. You didn't even know until you got to the infirmary that you'd been shot. You don't describe any burning feeling in your evidence or your statement. You had no idea you'd been shot. Therefore, it follows you had -- at the time you had absolutely no idea whatever where the shot was coming from that did wound you. That's right, isn't it? No idea at the time whatever.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I did have an idea. I was shot from Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your idea comes entirely from discussion and consideration after the event and putting together bits of knowledge with what you knew as a 12-year-old boy with what other people were telling you about what was going on in Mostar. That's the reality, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I know where I was and where the shot hit me from. I'm claiming this. I can't be a hundred per cent sure, but my opinion is that the bullet came from Stotina. You can see from the picture, from the photograph, that I was hit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can you offer any explanation of this? If you can't, say you can't. If you can, please, let's -- Their Honours know what it is. In some -- and I needn't trouble you with the details, but in some of the materials we -- which we have been supplied, and it's -- so everybody else knows what I'm talking about, it's an initial analysis of the incident involving you, it's said the distance from the firing point to the incident spot is approximately 800 to 900 metres. Just keep that figure in your head. We have -- needn't trouble you with the details but we have an expert report that deals with your incident and a number others that says specifically based on the analysis of the experts that the distance was 470 metres. So in all the material we've got we've got these two rather different distances. One to remind ourselves of 470 metres and the other of 800 to 900 metres. My question for you just, is are you in any position to give any explanation from your own knowledge of how those distances, those different distances emerged in the subsequent analysis of the incident in which you were shot?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And do you know whether the house from which you say shots were fired at you, do you know whether that is 470 metres or thereabouts from where you say you were shot, or is it more like 800 to 900 metres from where you say you were shot?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know. If I were to go there on foot, it would be 7 or 800 metres to Stotina, but the distance as the crow flies would be less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: As the crow flies, would it be more like 470, more like 800 to 900, or can't you say?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know how you make these measurements of distances as the crow flies. I can't make any comparisons. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no more questions, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Ms. Tomic, you certainly have some questions. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] I don't have any questions on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should have said, my client had asked if he could ask questions. I thought he would pop up straight away. I should have said so before the next counsel comes. I certainly wasn't wishing to take that opportunity away from him. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Cross-examination by the Accused Petkovic:

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, witness. Orucevica street, can it be seen from Hum or how much of it can be seen, if that is the case?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I don't know if you can see it from Hum. You have to go to a certain position to see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: What is it, if it's Hum?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I've never been on Hum I don't know how I can explain this to you. From Orucevica street from the place I was wounded at you can't see the top of Hum from the house. But if you move to the side you can see Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But location of the two as far as I can remember. I think you pointed to behind the house, the area behind the house, and by the house you can see the direction to Hum. Is that Hum?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you say you can only see how the Bulevar is entrenched in that area. You can see that from your house, but you can't see the top of him from your house?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But up to the top of the house, yes, you can see that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, I think that the house next to which I was standing can be seen from Hum but you can't see it from the place I was wounded. It's not possible to see it from the house. I can't be precise about that because I never had a look. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Could we have a look at the recording again? I don't know the number. Could we go back to the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could we see the 360-degree photograph again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. It's 9139. I'm very helpfully reminding myself and passing that along. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, this photograph shows the point at which you ran across the road?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Did you run from the right to the left?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Towards the rock wall next to the red doors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Very well. If you were running towards the stone wall where were you facing? Which part of you was facing upwards?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: The right part of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can we continue to view the photograph. Stop. To the left, can you see the slopes? Can you see the slopes?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Behind the branches?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: That's a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Which hill?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I think it's the Fortica hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Is that Fortica on Hum?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: No. Hum is behind this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Fortica is the front part in the direction of Mahala?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: No. It's across the river.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Very well. Across the river. Let's move on. Can we continue to view the photograph. Stop. The rocky part up there, what is it?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Judging by the height, this was photographed from a distance of about 50 metres. What's the name of the street?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: It's the high -- the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: But it's Hum?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It's behind the building from which you started to run?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you told us when marking the other photograph, you said that you could see Hum behind the area.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Well, I marked the second time I was wounded in the arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Let's continue to view the photograph. So we can conclude that Orucevica street can be seen from Hum and, as you yourself said, from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: And from Fortica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And from Fortica. I asked that for a good reason. Stop. Could you please zoom in. Can we zoom in a little more if possible? You said that this is the house to the left from which fire was opened on you?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Can you now mark it and point to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, you should have a marker. Mark the house from which you were shot at on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. This is in Sanction, and if the witness marks on the screen it won't show up. It will simply destroy the screen. I do have a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I thought Mr. Mundis had the means of doing everything. Apparently that's not the case. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Could you mark that house.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You've marked it with number 1. Put your initials down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you put your initials on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could we have an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes IC number 337. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, just one question of Fortica. When you were running, was Fortica to your left?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Who was on Fortica, do you know?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: I think the Serbs were there. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Ibrisimovic, any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. All the Defence teams have taken the floor. We haven't forgotten anyone. Mr. Mundis, any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions arising from the cross-examination. If I could be -- if I could have the witness be shown IC 00331, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Katica, you were shown some photographs. On these photographs, first of all, could you point to where the wound entered your body, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: On the left-hand photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could you please take the marker on the hard copy and draw the number 1 on the location where the bullet entered your body.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, the photograph on the right-hand side, what does that show, please?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: The exit wound.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please mark that with a number 2.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Katica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wonder if we can be absolutely clear that that is -- because it's just an observation but that is, I had assumed, and I hope there isn't any doubt about it but on the very left-hand edge of this picture is that gentleman's naval. I apprehend that there wouldn't be any doubt in Your Honours' minutes about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps we can do as we did with the witness last week. If this witness could simply stand up and point on his body where the bullet came in and where the bullet came out that might clarify this matter for once and for all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, if you could just stand up and, first of all, please point to the location on your body where the bullet entered your body.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And is that where the bullet exited your body? Sorry. And where the bullet exited your body.

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could get captures of that from the AV booth, please. Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. We're going to have a number but I have a question to ask. We saw the entry wound and the exit wound. You showed them to us. On -- according to what you know, did the bullet pass through your stomach or not?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, just to be clear, how do you know which one was the entry wound and which one was the exit wound?

utterances.speaker: DAMIR KATICA
utterances.text: The exit wounds, I suppose, are larger than the entry wounds. That's what they told me in the hospital as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, a number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 338.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That completes your testimony, Witness. I would like to thank you on behalf of my colleagues for having come to give testimony and to further the cause of justice. I'm now going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I turn to the representatives of the Prosecution, representatives in plural. Who is the next witness, and who is going to take him?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and to everyone in the courtroom. The next witness is Mr. Klaric, and I will be taking the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, in order to save time, with all due respect, as far as the statement signed by the witness and so on, whether there were any alterations, corrections, and so on, perhaps you could synthesise all that and ask it in one sentence so that the witness can answer yes or no rather than saying, did you sign the English version and then the answer is yes, and does it correspond to, et cetera, yes, and so on. Perhaps you could put that all in one sentence and have one answer from the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to be as efficient as possible. I can't say -- perhaps I'm doing a disservice to myself but I'm not sure that I can do that on my feet and cover all that in one question but I'll try to take it as efficiently as I can. Your Honour, I might just note before the Witness -- the witness comes in, there's been a lot of questions last week in particular -- and shown on previous occasions as well about the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Try, try.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. What I was saying, Your Honour, is there's been questions about the location of the confrontation line in Mostar. I'm sure I will be corrected if I'm wrong, but I don't think this is something --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not all of it in one sentence, just with respect to the statement, whether the statement was signed, whether there corresponds to the version, et cetera, et cetera. That's what I men.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I didn't think you meant the entire direct examination in one sentence, and I know I'm not that effective. Your Honour, if I might just before the witness comes -- Your Honour, if it might be helpful what I was going to say is the bundle of materials that has been circulated distributed in courtroom today among those is a map of Mostar that we have been frequently using in this case. What has been added to this particular map it's in the bundle and it is photograph for the record 060347 and I'm ask for a number to be given to it for the record purposes. It may have already been. If I may have the assistance of my case manager.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: While she's looking for that, Your Honour, I don't think there's any real dispute as to the location of the confrontation line in Mostar during -- during most of 1993 after the fighting on the 9th of May. The line remained relatively static in most situations. I'm not suggesting that there might not have been a movement of a few metres on any given day, but what we've done on this chart is add an orange line, you will see, just basically moving from -- I'll just describe it moving from left to right, including this strip -- well, let me back up and say I think the Chamber always knows and again I don't think it's disputed that the ABiH was able during this period to hold on to a small strip of land on the west side of the river. That strip of land continues from -- starting in Donja Mahala on the left side of the photograph, running along the street the Bulevar, through and into the main part of Mostar, through Spanish Square, zigzagging around beyond Spanish Square down to Santici Street. There is less certainty as to exactly where the line went from there this could be an area of some dispute or there could be an area where there was some movement of the line from time to time. And then continuing down to the river along -- across from the bridge there on the map and then continuing along the edge of the river. Now, I hope perhaps this is one -- unfortunately a few areas in the case where there might be some agreement between all the parties, if not, again, I'm sure I'll be corrected, but the Prosecution would say this is an accurate description and not particularly disputed but it may assist the Chamber. In my recollection of the various maps and photographs, for example that Mr. Praljak marked last week, it would seem to me that this line is generally consistent with the lines that various witnesses were putting on the maps and photographs presented by Mr. Praljak. I don't want to take too much more time on it now but I thought it would assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, you seem to be a specialist. The Prosecution has a map where in orange it marks the separation line. We can see that it follows the line of the Bulevar, then goes across Santic Street and seems to run along the Neretva River. Do you agree with the route? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] The map is true and correct, although it follows on towards the north and south, but, yes, there was this interrupted line, dotted line along Santic Street, and this is correct. I agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise, but with your permission I'd just like to say a few words. I think it would be important to emphasise that the division is the same of the area of control before the 9th of May, 1993, in order to avoid thinking that it was only after the 9th of May and the fighting that took place on that day that the area of responsibility was established as recorded on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Scott, is this before the 9th of May or after the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: To be perfectly transparent, I hadn't considered that aspect and it wasn't the point to get into a debate on the dates. I thought it was helpful to indicate that this was, I think, from a rough -- at least, if not before from the 9th of May forward through 1993 the relatively static position of the line. Without doing any further review of the evidence -- I don't mean to quibble with counsel, but I'm not prepared to say that the line was exactly this prior to the 9th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak -- or Mr. Petkovic for that matter. The line, was that before or after the 9th of May? THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to P 01978 of the 19th of April which is quite obviously before the 9th of May, and in point 1, 2, the points are defined and we say that they are as shown. So this was done on the 19th of April, and the Prosecution has P 01978, the document that was already shown in court, and in point 1, 2 it says how the line lies, how it stretches along that area, as controlling the area. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll check that out looking at document P 01978.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, would you please stand because you have to take the solemn declaration, but before you do so give us your name and date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Munib Klaric, born on the 20th of June, 1944.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have a current occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I work in Energopetrol, the company in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And what are you there? What --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm a warehouse worker or clerk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, have you ever testified in a court of law, national or international, about the events that took police in your country in the 1990s or is this the first time you're testifying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the first time that I am coming to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you now read the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just some information from me to start off with. You're going to answer questions first put to you by the Prosecution. Then you will be answering questions put to you by the Defence, and the Defence will have a total time of one hour. But I sincerely hope that the Defence will get through it in a much shorter space of time. Sir, if at any time during these proceedings you have any difficulties whatsoever, healthwise or any other kind, please don't hesitate to let us know and we will take a break. Having said that, you have the floor Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please. I am a diabetic. I do not have a right kidney, and I have a sick liver. So I might have to go to the toilet more often. I might have to ask to be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. If you're feeling ill, please let me know straight away.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I might, before we continue with the witness, just so we don't get too far away from it, I'm informed by the case manager that the exhibit number concerning the Mostar map with the orange confrontation line marked should be P 09891. Thank you. And if I could have the ushers's assistance, please, to move as quickly to have the bundle of documents put before the witness. Thank you very much. Your Honour, to provide the witness -- excuse me, the summary for this witness, it's quite brief but I'll read it into the record. On the 10th of October, 1993, at 1320 hours the witness went to get water from the Neretva River when he was shot in the heel by a sniper. This happened at the area called Podharemi in East Mostar. The witness was hit by a single shot. He was wearing civilian clothes. He was taken to the hospital and stayed there for six or seven days before he was operated because the doctors did not have time to treat him before, meaning that there were other higher priority patients. The witness thinks that the shot came from Stotina. And I might also indicate for everyone in the courtroom that this relates to incident number 10 in the expert report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The bundle of exhibits that has been put in front of you, Mr. Klaric, if you could find in that the very first exhibit which is Exhibit P 09862.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: 9862 you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. You will see in that exhibit, sir, two documents, one English language version of a statement that you signed immediately followed by the Bosnian language version of the same statement. As corrected by the president, Mr. Klaric, I'm going to try to take this as quickly as possible. I would like you to look, please, first of all at the English translation of the document. Or either one is fine. Is it correct, sir, that you gave an interview to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor on the 27th of June, 2001? If you look on the first page I will think you will see the date of the interview, if you need to. Do you see 27 June 2001?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, at the time that you were interviewed and you signed this statement initially in the English language, did you tell the truth and did you give your answers freely and voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Everything I say, Your Honours, I say of my own free will. Nobody forced me to say anything, and my approach was to tell the truth and nothing but the truth at my own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you'll look at the last page of the English statement, can you just confirm to us, please, that that contains your signature? Does it?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is it correct, sir, that at the time that you -- before you signed the document this document had been read back to you in your own language, you were satisfied with it, and it was at that time that you put your signature on the document? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, after you arrived in The Hague several days ago, Mr. Klaric, you were also given an opportunity to review your statement in the Bosnian language and, based on that review, can you tell the Judges is there any -- are there any corrections or additions that you would like to make to that statement?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: The statement I made I stand by. I have no additions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, if I were to take you through your statement in detail this afternoon and ask you questions related to all the information contained in your statement, would -- would the information contained in your statement be the answers that you would give to the Judges today?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would be true and the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Is it correct, sir, that in October 1993 you were living in the Tekija neighbourhood in East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: It is correct that I lived in Tekija and that that's where I live today as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just so there isn't any confusion on this because initially there may have been some for some of us, the location that you are going to describe to us today, the location where you were shot on the 10th of October, 1993, that location is not your home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No. That place is about 250 to 300 metres away from my home, and the street is called Haremi Kusalo [phoen], and my home is across the road from the tobacco factory in Marsal Tito Street, towards South Camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, sir. Now, can I ask you, your date of birth is 20 of June, 1943?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And you were shot on the 10th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So can we directly understand, sir, that at the time you were shoot you were 50 years old?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges approximately what time of day it was that you were shot? Was it -- well, let me ask you, was it 13.20 or 1.20 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Exactly at 1.20.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
