utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the statement describes some of the additional background including the clear visibility, the nature of the weather that day, and with the Court's permission I won't cover it again. Of course, others in the courtroom may, if they wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, what you were doing or had you been doing about the time that you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: As Mostar at that time was the only place that had water brought in by water trucks, I went to Neretva to bring in some water and -- or, rather, did not have water. I went down to the river to wash my clothes and bring in water. It was a nice day. I went down to the river, and I had a 50 litre canister and a smaller one of 20 litres and I went down several times to fill the canister, the large one and the small one, with water, and the last time that I went down to fetch water I was hit in my leg, and it was an entry/exit wound, and I fell down by the steps where I was supposed to come to that alleyway where there was shelter. And there were people who were in the houses. When they heard the shot two brothers came to my assistance and said, "Muna is -- has been wounded." And they pulled me out into the alleyway into the street and I was transferred to the institute of hygiene by a neighbour. I had to wait five more days to be operated because the wounded were being brought in from the front lines, so I was only operated on six days later. Is that sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Klaric, you ever very efficiently given us the most important information, I believe, in many respects. Thank you for that. Let me just ask you one clarifying question if you could answer this ever so briefly. You had indicated in your -- first part of your answer that because of the water situation in -- Mostar at the time was the only place that had had water in brought by water trucks. You then went on to talk about getting water from the river. Why did you not go and collect your water from the water supply trucks?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: It was a nice day, and the water trucks usually turned up in the afternoon, so I used the afternoon to go to -- down to the Neretva River at 13.20, since there wasn't any sniper shooting in town. Because we lived in a part of town where there was shooting almost round the clock, sniper shooting almost round the clock, and it would have been far better that I hadn't gone down to the water because I wouldn't have been here today, because it was sort of ill fated and what happened, happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me just ask you because the Judges have heard other fairly extensive evidence on this point, actually. Were you also aware at the time that the water tanker truck itself was often the target of either sniping or shelling?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So you went -- you went down to this location near the river and you said you were going down with a small container to bring water back up to larger container; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask that the witness please be provided with a clean copy of Exhibit P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment. There's a question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, I am sorry to interrupt you. I would only like to clarify one question here. In the written statement prepared by the witness, it was on page -- I believe it is page 1, that in the very last paragraph he has stated that there was only one shot and one hit. "I felt that I was hit in the heel." In the heel. Now, then, he made his statement here orally, then he mentioned that, and I quote him, "I was hit in my leg. I was hit in my leg." End of quotation. So I would like to ask the witness what was the place where his leg or heel was hit, and if he could show to us just in general way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I show you? Is that enough?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Prandler. If I could ask the usher's assistance to provide the witness with a copy of -- a clean copy of the -- it's previously been marked as 95 -- P 09517.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if could you please look at that map and orient yourself for at that moment. Could I ask you to make two markings on the map. The first marking -- please listen to my entire question before you begin making any markings. I would first ask you to mark the location where your house is on the map, if you can find it on the map, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Marsal Tito Street. That seems to be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You've just made a circle on the map. Can I ask you please to make the circle you're marking just a bit boulder if you could, please.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you to put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, could you also please indicate the location where you were at the time that you were shot in the heel?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: You can't see the road here. Have you got another map?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Not for current purposes, sir. If you say it's not on the map, just tell us it's not on the map and we'll go forward.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Well, it should be somewhere in this area. This is Hasan Brkic bridge, so around here Marsal Tito Street and then around here, you can't see those little streets.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. --

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This is the third street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, if I could ask the usher to move the maps around so everyone in the courtroom can see --

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I can't hear you now. It's very weak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Can you hear me now? Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: It's better now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And could I have -- ask the usher, please, again to move the map towards you. I think it would be toward you, madam. And perhaps it's the opposite. What we're trying to see is the very left-hand corner of the map. And now up a bit, please. All right. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This is Donja Mahala, and there's a new main road here. It should be to the left. This is where Stotina should be.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. You're getting a bit ahead of me. Can I ask you please, the marking you made a moment ago before we were moving the map around, you made a further map [sic] On photograph right -- or, excuse me, left of the one you marked number 1?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The second mark that you made, and I don't know, maybe that is a 2, but could you just confirm, did you put a 2 at that location then?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I ask you, sir, before we continue on with some of these events, aspects of this incident, in October 1993, at the time you were shot, were you in the military? Were you in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I only had a work obligation, something within the civilian protection. I had a work obligation. I wasn't an armija member. I worked within an organisation. I had a work obligation in a company. I didn't wear a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Were you at any time in 1992, 1993, or 1994 a member of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just tell the Judges what kind of clothes you were wearing at the time you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: A civilian uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, please, at the location where you were shot as you've marked it at location number 2 on the map you just marked, were there any military positions or installations in that vicinity at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No. No, never.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Excuse me, please, Mr. Scott. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, could you explain what a civil uniform looks like? It sounds a bit contradictory because normally you have -- either we have you were wearing civil clothes or a uniform, but certainly what you say makes sense. But could you help us to imagine what that looked like?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a civilian's uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A suit, a shirt, trousers. A soldier or policeman, a guard has a uniform. I'm a civilian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. So I came in a uniform to the Tribunal and didn't even know it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're in uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: May I just -- before we get too far away from it, may I ask that the map that has now been -- had the witness's markings on it please be given an IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes IC 338.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Continuing on in terms of -- you described your clothing. You indicated you were not in the military. Could you tell the Judges, please, at the time you were shot around 1.20 in the afternoon on the 10th of October, 1993, was there any -- was there any fighting or shooting going on in that area at the time?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: We'd go to get water when there was a lull. There wasn't a given time when the sniper would fire. People had to go to work. They had to carry out their work obligation, and the snipers opened fire that part of town day and night because we didn't have a protected part to get from my flat to the northern part of the house in the direction of Saric Harem and towards Podem Harem [phoen]. That's part of Mejdan. And we had to go through Mejdan from Zaharem [phoen] to reach the third part of the street called Kusalova Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Having all that in mind, sir, can I just ask you my question again and try to give a specific answer as best you can. At the time you were shot at the location you've indicated at approximately 1.20 in the afternoon on the 10th of October, 1993, was there any actual fighting or combat activity going on at that location, the location where you were shot?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, Witness, you've already shown us very graphically your foot. For the record, could we -- could I also ask that in the bundle of photographs that we've been using with these witnesses, the bundle is P 09220, and it's photograph number 05016240, and I understand it's page 21 in e-court of that exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could we have an IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 339.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we -- if it's quicker, I can put a copy on the ELMO. I believe it's page 21 of the e-court document. We don't have it. Do the other people have it in the courtroom? I don't have it on my screen. Now we do. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you showed us a few moments ago by removing your shoe and sock the wound that you suffered, the remains of that wound. Do you see that's depicted in this same photograph which is part of Exhibit P 09220 and has also been given the IC number 00339?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And is that be what we might consider an entry wound on the back of your heel? Just is it the entry -- does this show the entry wound on the back of your heel?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: There was an entry and exit wound to my heel, and the bullet passed through from the right to the left, but when our military -- military conscripts were to leave the Heliodrom, I fell on my balcony and I had a second operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I think --

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: To the right. It's here. And the first bullet inflicted an entry and exit wound, and this is the second bullet I received when I fell on the balcony. This was a sniper wound, and then I fell in the house. There were two occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, I'm going to need you please before you -- before you put your shoe and sock back on, I'm sorry, given what you've just told us could you please once again -- perhaps if you could stand, please, if you can keep your balance or we can get a good --

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: When I was wounded from Stotina, there was an entry and exit wound to this part. The second time I was operated here as a result of having fallen on the balcony. And here there was the entry and exit wound. The tendon was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, since the witness has very helpfully got his sock off, I wonder if we could very specifically see where the exit wound is because it's been a bit general with references to "here" without it being clear where "here" is. If he could simply put his finger on the exit wound that would be most helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't think you can see. We're not going to be able to get a camera on that particular --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want to come and have a look?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can see the entry wound. That's clearly what he's pointing to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or I could come to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I want to say it's not clear to me, Your Honour. It's -- I -- I -- if everybody in court knows, I still don't understand and see where the exit wound is. And that's all I'm asking, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't want the witness to get tangled up in his headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But, sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I wonder if the we might have the witness come around to the front of the witness stand, perhaps with the usher's assistance.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With the video camera being what the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, now, sir, come back?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I didn't want to make it that personal an invitation, Your Honour, but I'm flattered. He's behind the pillar from Your Honour. That's -- thank you very much indeed. That's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's the finest personal service I've had since I arrived in this place. I appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, perhaps the witness would be invited to show the whole arena from the centre, because I don't think if it's quite correct if one counsel got a good look.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I think so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's exactly what I intended but we got even more help than what we asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like you to do, please don't walk over to counsel, I'm sure he enjoyed it very much, don't go over to counsel, but with the usher's assistance please come in front of the witness stand. Please guide him very specifically, madam. Come out right in front of the witness stand. You'll have to leave your headphones. Leave his headphones. He's going to need his headphones. I think will. All right. Sir, we're improvising here and doing the best we can. I think there's an extension but I think it will take more time in the courtroom if we do it -- there we go. All right. Sir, what I'm going to ask you too do now, please, is once again please remove the shoe and sock of your left foot. I apologise, sir. I know this is very inconvenient and ...

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you could turn -- I'm sorry, Your Honour it's very difficulty don't want to be offensive to the witness. If you turn and lean your weight on the witness stand. Okay. Could I ask you please to lift a bit your -- no, no, sir. Stand a little closer, please. Now, if I could ask you, please, to move -- to raise your left foot a bit, just a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm sure the witness means no disrespect to the Court from his current position.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If it -- now, I don't know if -- can you lower your fit a bit, sir. Can you lower did to the floor a bit. Stop, stop. Stop there. Now, for everyone -- see -- is what we're seeing now in the back of your heel, sir, is that the entry wound of the sniper bullet that you received? Well, I think he knows. Hopefully he knows.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I'm not a medical orderly to be able to answer that question. My foot was operated on twice, once because of the wound from Stotina and the second time because I fell on the balcony, and the internal part or the inside part of my foot was wounded. I'm not able to provide you with a precise definition of what happened. I have shown you what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, there were two operations. The first one was performed because of the entry and exit wound and there was a second operation because he fell on the balcony. So he had two operations to his foot, but we have all seen the wound. We should now move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- to another subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could just ask, because there was a question from counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And, sir, if I could ask you once again to raise your foot a bit higher because there was a question of a scar or injury on the bottom of your foot. If I could ask you to raise your foot again, please. Now, stop there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honours, can everyone in the courtroom see that there is a circular scar on the bottom of his heel? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Thank you for your cooperation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We've spent an hour and 15 minutes on this matter so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I'll put a question to you because I want to go to the heart of the matter that concerns us. We saw where you were wounded. We saw the Donja Mahala area, too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Podharemi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as you know, did the ABiH have any soldiers in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not a single soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not a single soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I could ask you, on the map if you still have the map, which you marked before, which was Exhibit -- or was given IC number 00338, now, my next question to you, sir, and then I'll ask you to identify a marking, based on what you knew at the time, your knowledge of the area and what happened to you, did you have an understanding or belief as to where the shot came from that struck you on the 10th of October?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: As someone who was born in Mostar, as an inhabitant of the Mahala, well, I played football at Stotina. I would also swim in the Neretva River, and I know that that shot couldn't have come from anywhere else, only from that part of Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Sir, on that drawing, then, you made a map a few minutes ago. On the -- excuse me. On the mark that you're now saying you believe the shot came from Stotina, would you make a mark on the map using number 3.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, sir. Sir, it's correct, is it not, that in 2004 you were visited by an investigator and photographer from the Tribunal who made a short video clip with you; is that correct? Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we'd like to play the video clip Exhibit P 09140. If anyone cares to look at the brief very brief transcript it's on page 5 of 7 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you can watch this video, sir, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Klaric, to the best of your recollection, could you please indicate the location where you were shot? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you. Mr. Klaric, to the best of your recollection could you please assume the position you were in when you were shot? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you. Mr. Klaric, could you please point out where the shot hit you? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If we could run back through one -- to run part of it again, please, just very quickly. I'll tell you when to stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Klaric, to the best of your recollection could you please indicate the location where --"

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Actually, we can stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can I just ask you, after you were shot at the location you pointed to just a minute ago in this clip, could you tell the Judges what you did immediately after that? Did you seek cover? Did you try to move in any particular location, and if you did can you show us on this photograph as best you can the direction, location where you moved?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I crawled as far as this protected area, this sheltered area, the small step you can see here. There's an arrow that you can see. I reached this sheltered area and then two brothers of mine took me to the hygiene institute, the institute of hygiene.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. So that the record is clear, when you say up in the sheltered area, are you talking -- would it object on the photograph -- if everyone's looking at the photograph it would be to the left of where you're standing now up to the step? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This part here to the right. The left side and this part. I reached the sheltered area to make sure that the sniper wouldn't hit me a second time. It wouldn't possible for him to hit me there any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I think a different photograph, Your Honour, might make it clear rather than take too much additional time with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, the next thing I would like to do, please, is show you what we are calling in the courtroom a 360-degree photograph. You may recall that at the time that after the video was taken a tripod was set up at the location you indicated and then a circular photograph was made. What I'd like to do, please, is first I just want you to look at the entire photograph as we play it the first time. Then I will play it for you a second time, but just the first time I want you to orient yourself, please. All right. We started approximately there. All right, sir, at this time I'd like to do it again, and this next time that we do this can you please be watching for the location of the place where you think that the shot came from. Don't -- don't start yet. And then I'll just ask you to tell us to stop.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Go back, go back, go back. More, more. It's somewhere here, a bit further back. To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: A little more. You can see a house here and a hill. Go further to the left. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Can -- now, hold on there for a moment, please. Hold on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. Just looking for ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While you're look, we have some questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, while the Prosecution is looking for its document, I'd like to know the following: It's -- was this house inhabited, the one in front of which you were wounded at the time of the event?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you didn't -- you weren't afraid of -- of snipers? Didn't the owner of this house fear shots from snipers when you went there to collect water? They didn't say anything about being afraid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only the owner but ought inhabitants of Podharemi and Marsal Tito Street were all afraid every day, and we expected someone to die every day. Not only the owner of the house where this event took place, because the area I lived in, Tekija in particular, well, that area was under fire, under sniper fire day and night. My flat is on the left on the Neretva River across from the tobacco factory. The water and food was transported through my flat because it was the quite elevated and was the only protected part at the time. Everywhere else from the -- one of the buildings to my building there was an area that wasn't protected, and from the Kolonija area that goes in the direction of Sokol, well, they passed through that passageway -- rather, they opened fire. Snipers opened fire in that area. Is that sufficient?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You pointed to a house in the photograph. We can see it clearly. Before you were wounded, had shots already been fired from that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm telling you that they opened fire from that part of Stotina and from elsewhere not only on Tekija but on the entire town. I served in the army in '66 and '67, so I didn't really -- but I didn't really carry a rifle frequently so I don't know much what the range of weapons is. I don't know if I could take a rifle apart right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before -- the question was very precise. Did the inhabitants in that area know that there was a -- a sniper in the house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, there could have been a snipe near any of the houses, not just in one of the houses. Not just in that one. In Stotina there could have been a thousand and one snipers, not just the one sniper who wounded me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Scott, the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. If I could have the usher's assistance, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to show you now --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm going to show you now a still photograph of roughly the place you stopped us on the video, and what I'd like to do now is -- if you can please take the marker. Please look carefully. Don't rush to make the markings particularly quickly, but look at the photograph, please, and then make a mark, draw a circle around the location where you believe the shot came from that hit you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to object to this. There is absolutely no foundation whatsoever to suggest that this witness can have any knowledge about where the shot came from. It's obvious from his testimony that he more or less had his back to where the shot came from, and an attempt to say that it must have come from this building or that building is -- is absolutely speculation in its purest form.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I can't agree, Your Honour, with that. I mean, again the witness has given us his knowledge of the events and the location at the time, what was known about the operations in this area, and, with all respect, I think it goes to weight but it's no different than the evidence given by a number of these witness, with all candour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, he just said in response to a question from Your Honour that there could have been a sniper near any of the houses, not just in one of the houses. He said that explicitly in a question -- in response to a question from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, Mr. Murphy is a hundred per cent right, Your Honour, and we whole-heartedly support his objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Please continue, Mr. Scott, and we'll see in due course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Perhaps for the record it is important to say that the witness has not said he could have been shot at from any houses. He said a sniper could have been in any of the houses. I think there's a distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Precisely, Judge Trechsel, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Perhaps that might be so, Your Honour, but nonetheless Mr. Scott is to lay a foundation for -- when asking a witness to give this kind of opinion. He's presumably going to use this as a basis for asking his expert witness in a day or two to give us an opinion as to where the shot came from a very specific location, and it's important that the Trial Chamber understand there is absolutely no foundation for in whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: If Mr. Scott allows me to associate myself with Mr. Murphy's objection. Could we observe, Your Honour, this is a 92 ter witness which the statement he has confirmed is important to look at and the vagueness of -- it's the fourth but last paragraph in his statement he uses the word "suppose," which entirely supports of what Mr. Murphy has said. It is supposition, and it's not to the Prosecution to go so far beyond a 92 ter statement without a foundation and add this specific material. If they want to go under 92 ter they, within reason, should be stuck with 92 ter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's completely -- that's -- Your Honour, that's completely unfair I'm afraid from Mr. Stewart. The word "suppose" could be -- indicates "I believe," indicates that's an English phrase, and I think he can suppose and indicate the photograph where he supposes that the shot came from, knowing -- having grown up in the area, having known where certain sniper locations were to be during this time, from his own injury from where he was standing at the time -- located at the time from where he was shot from crawling out of the line of fire up between the two building the witness can give his view just the other two witnesses have given their view as to where he believes the shot came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I suppose it comes in a whole sentence, Your Honour, not just that word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart, the Judges will deliberate and weigh up everything and come to a reasonable conclusion as to where this sniper shot came from. But before the Judges can arrive at a conclusion, we must have all the elements at hand. And that is the object of the examination-in-chief and indeed the cross-examination as well. Now, Witness, you were hit in the heel. We saw that. In your opinion, where did the shot come from?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Can you turn your back to where you know the shooting came from? If you can, I'll give you the Nobel Peace Prize. I was walking towards the house and the sniper hit me, so I know where it came from. Now, you're the experts and you ought to know. Judging by the wound, the shot came from Stotina. It hit me from Stotina a had I known they would shoot at me I would have taken cover, but I had my back turned towards that area. I was carrying a canister. How should I know where the shooting came from? It's an assumption.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So in Stotina there are a number of houses, aren't there, a number of houses there? Did you think it came from a specific house or you don't know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't be specific. I can just assume, because each of those houses was a potential sniper place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, based -- based on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, Mr. Karnavas. What -- it's clear he doesn't know where the shot came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's the whole point. I think here we're wasting valuable time with a witness. Granted, he was hit. We don't know whether it was a shooter, a sharpshooter, whether there was a ricochet, whether this was somebody who was actually sniping at the gentleman. We do know he was injured, and we apologise for having to bring him here for that purpose. But other than that we are not advancing anywhere by this pure speculative approach, and I don't think it's fair to the Defence given that the Prosecution has the burden of proving their case at a standard of proof beyond a reasonable doubt, and this is not proof beyond a reasonable doubt. So I suggest that we thank the gentleman and send him about his way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I disagree, Your Honour we're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Mr. Scott, I'm sorry to interrupt you again, but really I fear that we should make up our mind what we are going to ask from the witness. We, as far as I know, at least the Bench doesn't want to ask the witness exactly from which house the shot has come. We would like to ask the witness, as he already stated before, from which direction did the shot come, which direction. So therefore he already said several times that the shot came from Stotina. Now I would like to ask the witness if he could just show to us in general that in his view from which -- which kind of buildings the shot might have come. We do not ask you to say that it is exactly this or that house. We are asking you to show the direction which in your view the shot was fired. It is what I would like to ask you to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll draw a circle round the location of Stotina. Whether it was from a building or which part exactly I can't say, but if you bring me a map, on the screen I will draw a circle round the locality that we call Stotina. But what building specifically, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's have a photograph, and could you draw a circle round the area you consider the shot came from. Draw a large circle round the area.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour, and I think it's been very unfair to this witness not to have given him the opportunity some minutes ago to answer that. That is exactly the markings that he has indicated to the Prosecution before. The witness never indicated it was a particular building. He said it was at Stotina up on this elevated area and that is his testimony and I think the witness has been confused and interrupted from being able to give the answer he just gave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just tell the truth. So you can't confuse me. I won't let myself be confused. Don't worry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know if we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 341. I would like to make a correction. Since the number IC 338 was given twice, on page 53, line 21, it should be IC 340.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, just so the record's clear, on page 80, line 19 through 24, Mr. Scott directed a specific question to the witness as to where the location that he believed the shot came from. So, Your Honour, for him to represent that we are being unfair to the witness is absolutely outrageous.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's exactly the question I put to the witness, and the witness now answered after 15 or 20 minutes of arguing.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I can ask you to look, please, next at another photograph that I'll show you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Put that on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if -- can you tell us, sir, what we're looking at now? Is this looking up from the steps where you pointed out? In the short video clip, you bent over and pointed to some steps. Are we now looking up into the direction of where those steps go between the buildings?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This is called Gusav Soka [phoen], a small street. This is the bottom of the steps emerging at Haremi, the lower part here. Below is the plateau where I was standing towards the Neretva River. Is that sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is that the area, sir when you said a few minutes ago that you climbed then or crawled further up between those buildings, is this showing the location where you crawled after being shot?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: The lower part of the steps, that's where there was a bit of shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask for an IC number for this photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 342.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance to please put 00 -- IC 00341 back on the screen. Thank you. If we can go out and show as much of the picture as possible, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can, using this photograph, when you came up from the river, your last trip up from the river prior to the time you were shot, we see on the right part of the photograph what looks like it could be a sidewalk or some sort of a gravel path or open area. Now, with reference to that, can you indicate approximately where you came up from the river before you stepped onto that path?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: There was a stone path and then a path with cement. So I came to the very corner of the alleyway or path, and that's where the sniper hit me, as I showed you on that first photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: But before you got to the corner, as you came up to the river now, could you put a marking on the picture, if you can, as to where you were when you first came up from the river?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you, Mr. Klaric.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm told by my case manager that we've come up on the time. I think we're very, very close to being finished, but -- well, I'm in the Court's hands. I can probably finish in two or three minutes or we can take the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead and complete your examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in the bundle of exhibits, if I could just ask you please to look at -- if you can find P 06980, 6980.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: 6980, you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please. If you have that, sir, I'm directing your attention to the -- well, please look at the Bosnian language version of that document. Can you just simply confirm, sir, is this a record from the Mostar war hospital indicating the treatment of the wound that you've described to us this afternoon when you were -- your sniper wound that you received on the 10th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This document --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Sir, my -- I've directing you to the wrong number. It's my fault. My apology to the courtroom. If I can ask you please to look at 6316. I turned to the wrong tab, sorry. 6313 -- 6316. My question to you is the same, sir. Could you tell us if this is a record of the Mostar war hospital concerning the sniper wound that you received on the 10th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. President, the rest of the bundle contains a number of ongoing medical records showing the continuing treatment of that wound for some time. Unless it's disputed, I don't think it's necessary to put those exhibits into evidence. And that concludes my examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. It's 10 to 6.00, or almost, and we resume at 6.10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 6.10 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Theoretically we have 50 minutes more. I implore the Defence to get through it by 7.00 in order to release the witness of his obligations. Mr. Karnavas, are you going to start off?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I wasn't going to, but I have no questions for the gentleman. We wish to thank him for coming here to The Hague. We apologise he had to come all this way just to tell us that you couldn't locate from which direction the shots came from. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: We have no questions. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak has a few questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good evening, Your Honours. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good evening, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Good evening, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't have just a few questions. I have as many as I need to ask within the time I have been allotted. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] May I ask Madam Usher to take some papers over there to the witness that I'd like to have placed on the overhead projector in this order, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, Mr. Klaric, before we start looking at the documents on your table, tell me the following, please, as to the best of your knowledge: You're from Mostar. You know Mostar well. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, before the beginning of the war, just before the war when the Yugoslav People's Army arrived and the reservists and so on, at that time did many people try to procure weapons in one way or another because they felt the war was coming on?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I didn't know about that. May I make a comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, you may not.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No. With respect to the arrival of the Jugo armada. I was at work at the time, and you know where the south part of Mostar is, you know that very well, Mostar number 4, the petrol station there, and Mr. General Praljak, I was the first to be taken to Buna first. Us three Bosniaks worked on the petrol pump. Three Serb, orthodox, worked on the left petrol pump. Since my writing is not that good, my colleague Dragan Maksimovic was inside and he wrote out bills and took in payment. I felt the work of the engine and I felt that it was a diesel engine, and I sent him to the petrol station for gasoline, and when I sent him there he just came out and cocked an automatic rifle at me. And there was a whole table with money. And the late Ali Podmeki [phoen], he was my colleague, one of mine. The other colleague, Radim Mansuric [phoen], works today still at number 2 with Asim, Asim Dzulejman, over there, that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness. I'm sorry. Witness, I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sure you have perhaps more very dramatic and interesting and important stories to tell but here we are limited to where you were shot in your foot, in your heel. So unfortunately we should -- you should not --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: It's okay. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Klaric, I could listen to you for hours. I would be very ready to listen to you, but unfortunately my time is very limited here. So I have to clear up the situation with you. So please help me out to the best of your ability.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you a question? Just short. If I knew who that person was who hit me in the heel, I would have a cup of that Mostar coffee of ours with him, and I'd forgive him, but I would not forget. Now, you tell me. That's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We can go that far. I can't go that far.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I'm not going far. I'm just asking a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, I don't know why I'm here questioning you about your injury, but there you have it. That's what the situation is. Now, do you know what an M-48 rifle is?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Do you know that it does individual shots, shoots individual shots? Do you know what a semi-automatic rifle, the so-called PAP, P-A-P is?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No, I don't I've never had it in my hands. Quite right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, I'll go slowly. Have you heard of an automatic rifle produced by the Crvena Zastava factory?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: All I know is the M-48 rifle that I had in my hands. Don't ask me about anything else with respect to weapons. I know nothing else about other types of weapons, not a pistol not a carbine, nothing else. I wasn't interested in anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, in light of the time constraints and the nature of the witness, I suspect -- let me suggest, Your Honour, I think we might get more -- be more productive for the witness to go to the events on the 10th of October. He is the one that started us talking about Yugoslav army in 1991, 1992, et cetera, et cetera. Can we go straight to the sniping incident on the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Mr. Praljak if you go through all types of weaponry with this witness, it might be interesting. But apart from the M-48, he knows nothing else. So move on. We're going to have a witness coming in to talk to us about things like that, so it will be simple for you to ask the expert witness your questions. What we're interested in is the wounding, who did the shooting, and from what direction or from what locality. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Judge Antonetti, Mr. Scott, everybody who comes in here, all the witnesses who come into court here say that a sniper shot. That is crystal clear. It's he a crystal clear statement, after which the witness goes on to say that apart from an M-48 rifle he cannot differentiate between any other weapon. So my logical question is, how does a sniper bullet sound when it is shot if compared to any other individually shot bullet from an M-48 rifle, a .762 automatic rifle, a Heckler rifle, an M-16 rifle, a semi-automatic rifle, the Heckler from the USA. So how can somebody today here in the courtroom either of -- on the part of an expert witness or a witness can differentiate an individual shot from a sniper shot? Because we've been hearing for days here that there were sniper fire, and all we know is that the gentleman was hit in the way in which he was hit and wounded, and then I am being questioned the right of asking how he can recognise a sniper shot. Just I asked -- as I asked the doctor who was a witness what the difference is between a sniper wound and -- very well. Let's have sketch number one, please. Can we show the witness sketch number one.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, this is a map that the Prosecution and we have agreed represents the demarcation line between the ABiH and the HVO. You can see Donja Mahala here. Above Donja Mahala in green you can see the Hum hill; is that correct have a look. Have a look at what you were looking at.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I have to put a different pair of glasses on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you please place it on the ELMO so that everyone can see. Place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: So you're referring to this left part here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, what you were pointing to, is that the Hum hill?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, for me as an inhabitant of Mostar, everything from Stotina to the -- to what they call the Hrvoje cinema is Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Could you mark Hum there.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's right. Raise the image a bit. You can see the Hasan Brkic bridge and to the left there should be Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Not to the left but to the right. Downstream, downstream. Downstream is right, Mr. Praljak, my house is to the left from the tobacco factory. You should look in the direction of the flow of the Neretva. Is this how the Neretva flows? Donja Mahala is to the right. Hum is to the right, and Brkic bridge and Tekija is to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Klaric, place the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We won't get a good transcript if the speakers are overlapping, and I think it's unfair to the language assistants who help us so much every day, so if they could please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite right. Answer Mr. Praljak's question and give the interpreters sufficient time to do their work. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Klaric, please mark the location of Stotina with an arrow.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And could you write down number 2 there. Put your initials on it below and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's have an IC number. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be IC number 343. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's move on and have a look at the next photograph, at the next image. Could we turn it around so we have the Neretva in front of us. That's right. This is the location at which you were wounded. The Neretva is down below, and then vertical to the Neretva we have the street towards Sakic Harem and we have houses to left and right. This is what you indicated. Were you facing these steps, these stairs?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was facing the stairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you mark the stairs with an arrow, and this is the direction you were facing in?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Right down number 1.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The Neretva River flows towards the right. Isn't that correct? Now, where is Stotina here? Where did the bullet that hit you come from? Indicate the direction that the bullet came from.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's the Neretva, sir.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: You said the direction. There is -- I just marked Stotina to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. But use an arrow to indicate the direction from which the bullet came.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This is the direction that the Neretva flows in, and this is Stotina. You won't confuse me, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm not trying to. Let's have a look at the next image and could we have an IC number for this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you put your initials on the document and we'll have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 344. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's a broad sketch. Please mark the location at which you were standing when you were hit by the sniper.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: With an arrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With an X.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mark it with a number 1.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And indicate the direction from which the bullet that hit you came in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Two and an arrow.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: In your direction. The arrow -- the arrow must point in your direction.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And please could you signed that?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 345. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Could we turn the photograph around.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, in the lower right-hand corner, can we see the houses in Stotina? I'm referring to the lower right-hand corner. The three house we can see there, is it Stotina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I can see Brkica bridge as a reference point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please take your time to examine the image.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I can't see the bridge here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The bridge is here.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Where? I can't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Have a look at the Neretva and to the right you have a large bridge.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's the Hasan Brkic bridge; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the houses near your hands, is that Stotina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes. Those are the houses in the area of Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mark them.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: The houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Just the houses.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I had a good friend, Franjo, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mark that area with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Have a look at the area near the Neretva River now, and mark the location of your house -- or, rather, not your house but the site at which you were hit. Next to the Neretva on the left bank there are two houses, number 9 or 10 marks the spot.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I can't see the streets here. I can't see what I should encircle because of the bushes. I quite clearly pointed out facilities in this photograph, but I can't find my bearings here. I can't find my bearings here in these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Let's leave that. This was the photograph that was made by an expert. I didn't take this photograph and that's why I thought you would be able to use the photograph?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Klaric, roughly speaking, would you be able to locate the area that you were wounded at in the photograph? Approximately speaking, could you give us a rough indication?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I mark this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Yes. Mark it with an X and number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mark the spot with an X and number 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've marked it with an X.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, could you give the witness a better pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. And your initials.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is where I went to swim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 346.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for the registrar. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Are these the houses in Stotina that we saw a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I haven't been up there for 30 years. I can only assume that this part here -- well, as a child I used to play ball there, but now that I'm 64 I can't go 30 years back in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Klaric --

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If there's something you can't remember, just say so.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether this is Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Excellent. Let's move on then.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I can't recognise it from this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let's move on. The next photograph, please. Do you recognise this house in Stotina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move on. Let's have a look at the next one. If you imagine Stotina, is this the view from Stotina, the view of the Hasan Brkic bridge and the new buildings that were constructed there? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I think it should be a little more to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is one part of the area. In your opinion, was this photograph taken from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: This is the crossroads where -- at Hasan Brkic that heads off in the direction of the Stotina. So Stotina should be here, but you can't see that location here. I know what I'm saying very well, Mr. Praljak. This is a new road that heads in the direction of Sokol, and every day I would go there and my bike. I'd cycle for 20 kilometres, but you can't see Stotina here. I don't know whether this is the right document, the right image.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. You don't know whether this other photograph was taken from Stotina, the one we're looking at now?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I assume that this could have been photographed from Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: It could have been?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No. This is the park that heads in the direction of airport.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is this taken from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: It could have been taken from a plane.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Have a look at the new photograph. Was this photograph taken from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak, I don't know where it was taken from. I'm not a photographer. You're showing me some photographs --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I'm asking you --

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Let's move this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: All the photographs you have shown to me, well, don't show them to me. Show me what I have produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please, let's have another look at IC 342.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: I'm not interested in these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: IC 342. And could we have the 360-degree photograph prepared. So this is the street, and you said that you were facing these steps when you were wounded; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you mark the direction you were facing with an arrow and could you put your initials on the document. Let's have an arrow and your initials and number 1.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And now could we have a look at the 360-degree photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have a number, please. The registrar has told me that this photograph already has the IC number 342.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do we have a photograph with these arrows and with the witness's initials? That's what is particular to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, in that case let's have a new number for this photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be then IC number 347. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Could we please have the 360-degree photograph, the IC document that was a Prosecution document. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] The 360-degree document is P 09139, if we may be of assistance. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We'll have a look at that 360-degree photograph. Witness, I wouldn't even think of saying that you weren't wounded, that you didn't suffer much, but I'm just trying to establish something on the basis of what you yourself have said, on the basis of what has been said here. I want to establish whether the way in which you were wounded is the way in which it has been described, because if you are facing the steps and Stotina is 30 degrees from your axis, and if on the basis of the wounds one can conclude that the entry and exit wound is at an angle of 60 degrees, well, then you, too, would have to ask yourself where the shot was fired from since your wound is at an angle of 60 degrees whereas Stotina is quite to the right of you down the Neretva. And this is why I would like to have a look at the 360-degree photograph again. P 0 -- that was the P number? That's the question. Not whether you were wounded but from how and from where.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: General, I'm not a general like you are, so I can't know where the but came from. All I know is that I was wounded. As to the angle, as to where it came from, I don't know. My heel is the corpus delicti.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's why we're here so that we can assist each other to establish the truth. No one puts your wounding into question, but we want to establish how you were wounded. On the basis of where you were standing we want to see where the bullet could have come from, the bullet that wound you, and that's why I wanted to have a look at the 360-degree photograph, P 09139. What is surprising is that the Prosecution hasn't proceeded in this manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, we did proceed in it and it's unfair to the witness to mischaracterise his testimony. He testified that he came up the side of the river and he showed on this exact photograph, that he turned on the path and had his back to Stotina. That's at page 81 and page 83 of the transcript. So it's completely unfair for Mr. Praljak to characterise the evidence the way he wants to characterise it as opposed to what the transcript says.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott, even if he was facing Stotina the entry and exit wound at 60 degrees should demonstrate something here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak has the right to ask the witness to have a look at the 360-degree photograph and then he will put his question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We have no control over it, Your Honour. But apparently there is a technical problem. It's ready to play for us, and so -- do we have it? Play it, I guess. Hit play and see what happens. Your Honour, apparently it can't be played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is a problem. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript I would like to say that the photograph quite clearly shows that behind Mr. Klaric's back one can see the Hum hill, and it's a lot more likely that --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak is purely giving testimony. I'm sorry, Your Honour, it's pure testimony by Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you have heard what General Praljak said. When we looked at the 360-degree photograph we saw Stotina, but we also saw Hum on it. Now, could you perhaps have been shot by a bullet coming from Hum hill? Would that have been possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, number one Judge, I said a moment ago that I'm not a military expert. I have come here an as a wounded man and shown you my opinion, given you my opinion as to where the bullet could have come from. Now, had it come from Hum, then my heel would have been blown away altogether and I would not have an entry/exit wound from right to left. I had an entry exit wound from right to left, if you were able to see that properly on the photograph. So there's no logic that it came as the general is saying, from that area. It came from -- of course, now, I don't -- I'm not a military man to know what the elevations are and so on. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The bullet came from top to bottom, so I'm speaking at an angle of 50 to 60 degrees from top to bottom. Let's have a look at that again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, in the meantime can you recall, can you tell us whether when your heel was hit you had your foot fully on the ground or lifted in a -- in a position which one assumes when one walks? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that point in time I had fallen from the shot. I fell down and I was own the ground, and then I crawled to the second step to take shelter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I did not put the question properly. The moment when the bullet hit you, was your foot on the ground with the heel or was the heel elevated? Maybe you do not remember. Then just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can't decide. I can't say. I really can't say with any certainty, so I don't want to say anything I'm not very certain of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Klaric, you were hit. Nobody is challenging that. Somebody hit you in the heel. But look at this here. We have Stotina. Let's go round now. Imagine the position of your body and the position of your leg and the entry/exit wound. Look at the 360-degree photograph. Let's rotate the photograph, and look and see where it is most probable where the bullet came from. We're going from Stotina to Hum. We can see Hum and the buildings controlled by the BH army. This is Donja Mahala. You'll agree that was under BH army control, was it not? We see Hum. Is it true? Is that Hum? Stop. Stop there. So now you -- your back is turned towards this, because if you are turned -- facing the Neretva then your back is facing this area here. You are facing -- your back is turned to the Neretva River.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: These are the buildings at Cekrk in Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: So I'm -- my back is turned towards those buildings. And behind those buildings is Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. Hum and Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Do you know how long Stotina's been there for? Do you know where the catering establishment of Smajo was? Let me explain to you. You're trying to trick me here. You're trying to catch me out with only tricks. Smajo's cafe was a hundred metres that way and then Hum was the other side. So I don't know what point we've reached. Mr. Prlic, you don't have to whisper to Mr. Praljak. He's clever enough himself to be able to ask the questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have taken the solemn declaration to tell the truth and nothing but truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're showing yourself up because you seem to be a bit upset. Now, the Judges sitting in front of you, the four Judges, we have to determine in a quasi-scientific method where the shot came from. We know that you were facing the steps which means that your back was turned towards what we see on the photograph now when it's being rotated. Now, as the Judges, as professional Judges up here on the Bench, I cannot exclude that the shot could have come either from the buildings that we can see in front of us or from the hill. So we have to know ultimately on the basis of all the elements you give us where the shot could have come from. Do you understand that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we have it then. Now, in order to facilitate our task, the Prosecutor asked you questions. You asked -- answered those questions, and the accused has the right to answer [as interpreted] you questions, too, and you have to answer them. And then afterwards the Judges will gather together and confer and deliberate and reach a conclusion as to where the shot came from. Having said that, Mr. Praljak, please continue. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] On the photograph we're looking at now, can we state that the witness said that his back was turned towards this building and this hill that we call Hum hill? Is that possible?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's nothing on the screen, no picture on my screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You haven't got a photograph up on your screen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Usher, would you go and have a look, because there doesn't seem to be a photograph on the witness's screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's just come on. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me repeat my question. Is it correct, and you've already told us this in response to a question from Judge Antonetti, that your back was facing this building and this hill when you were hit up by the steps. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we record this in some way? Can we mark this in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I make a comment? These are buildings in Donja Mahala. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, they are buildings in Donja Mahala.

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: So they're not at Stotina.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers refrain from overlapping, please. It is impossible to translate in this way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have an IC number for the photograph.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC 348. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And my last question: Witness, Mr. Klaric, do you know that at the time you were wounded, behind these buildings we see here was the BH army line facing the positions of the Croatian Defence Council that were up in the hill? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MUNIB KLARIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You don't. Then I have no further questions. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
